cve_candidates.description: rpcbind and libtirpc memory exhaustion via crafted GETPORT/CALLIT flood; causes denial of service through resource exhaustion. Metasploit module available (ExploitDB 41974.rb).
rpcbind CALLIT procedure UDP crash PoC — abuses the indirect-call RPC procedure with a malformed UDP packet to crash the rpcbind daemon.
Use-after-free vulnerability in libtirpc svc_dg_getargs() — potentially exploitable for remote code execution, though rarely weaponised in practice.
PMAPPROC_DUMP amplification: rpcbind responds to a small spoofed UDP request with a large service listing, enabling DDoS reflection/amplification with a bandwidth factor of 7–28x.
IKEv1 Aggressive Mode leaks the pre-shared key (PSK) hash without prior authentication. The hash is recoverable offline via dictionary or brute-force attack using ike-scan.
Cisco IOS/IOS XE IKEv1 fragmentation information disclosure — unauthenticated attacker can read process memory contents. Cisco-specific; applicability depends on device vendor.
NetBIOS Name Service broadcast poisoning via Responder: attacker responds to NBNS queries with a spoofed IP to capture NTLMv1/v2 hashes for offline cracking or relay attacks.
SambaCry — remote code execution via shared library injection over an exposed Samba writable share. Exploitable if Samba services are reachable through RPC/NetBIOS.
SIGRed — wormable Windows DNS Server RCE via malformed SIG record. Critical if target is running Windows DNS. CVSS 10.0.
Kaminsky DNS cache poisoning attack — exploits weak transaction ID randomisation to inject forged DNS records and redirect traffic.
DNS ANY/RRSIG amplification: if configured as an open resolver, ANY queries return large responses to spoofed sources, enabling DDoS reflection with a 50–100x bandwidth amplification factor.
Unauthenticated UDP syslog accepts forged log messages from any source. Attackers can inject false log entries to cover tracks, trigger SIEM false positives, or corrupt audit trails.

attack_surface_summary: Target 172.20.0.2 (redteam_easy-target-1) is confirmed alive via ARP but exposes zero TCP services — all 65,535 TCP ports return RST, and HTTP/HTTPS are unreachable. The attack surface is exclusively UDP-based, with six ports in open|filtered state (53, 111, 137, 162, 500, 514); no service version banners were captured due to the host rate-limiting UDP probes. The most critical initial access paths are: (1) rpcbind/portmapper on UDP/111, which has multiple Metasploit-ready DoS exploits and a potential RCE via CVE-2015-7236, and whose PMAPPROC_DUMP response can also enumerate all registered RPC services to reveal additional hidden services; (2) ISAKMP/IKE on UDP/500, which may be a VPN gateway susceptible to IKEv1 Aggressive Mode PSK hash extraction and offline cracking (CVE-2002-1623); and (3) NetBIOS-NS on UDP/137, enabling LLMNR/NBNS poisoning via Responder to harvest NTLMv2 hashes. DNS on UDP/53 poses a secondary risk as a potential open resolver (amplification) or as a Windows DNS RCE target (CVE-2020-1350 / SIGRed). Post-compromise privilege escalation would depend on what RPC services are registered with portmapper (enumerable via rpcinfo) and whether captured credentials can be cracked or relayed. The syslog service (UDP/514) enables log injection for defence evasion. Recommended immediate follow-up: rpcinfo -p 172.20.0.2 to enumerate RPC programs, ike-scan --aggressive 172.20.0.2 to test IKEv1 PSK leakage, and Responder on the local interface to capture any NBNS traffic.
